subject: Re: Vendor change: overage smoothing & exit-credit ladder
messages:
From: Kate Owens <kate.owens@nimbusai.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor change: credits & overage smoothing?

Hi Rishi,

We’re running a quick evaluation of alternatives and I wanted to check whether Redwood has any standard approaches for two things that keep coming up on our side: (1) an "exit credit ladder" for customers moving from an incumbent to you, and (2) an overage-smoothing option so our finance team doesn't see big spikes during the cutover month.

Short background: Nimbus AI currently has a 24/7 product in prod using another vendor. We expect a 60–90 day ramp if we switch. Procurement asked for an example proposal showing how you’d structure credits + temporary overage smoothing for the first 3 billing cycles. I attached the RFP and an anonymized usage sample.

Can someone on your team share a couple of concrete packaging options (preferably with quick arithmetic) we can show the CFO this week?

Thanks,
Kate
Kate Owens
Head of Platform Partnerships
Nimbus AI
Attachment: Nimbus_RFP_q2.pdf

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Owens <kate.owens@nimbusai.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 08:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor change: credits & overage smoothing?

Hi Kate — thanks for the context and the RFP. Laura and I pulled the usage sample and sketched three short options below. Quick ask: can you confirm average monthly token volume and peak-day 95th percentile for the last 3 months (or point us to the sample CSV column that has daily tokens)? That will let us put real numbers against these options.

High-level options (ballpark illustrations):

Option A — Exit-credit ladder (recommended for revenue-protection)
- 3-month ladder: 40% credit month 1, 25% month 2, 10% month 3 applied to service fees only
- Customer pays usage at list; credits applied to invoice; no egress credits
- Pros: preserves unit economics for Redwood, visible immediate relief for Nimbus

Option B — One-time buyout + short-term commit
- One-time fixed buyout to offset migration costs (covers migration services + overlap) + 3-month committed baseline with overage smoothing at 50% of list for overages
- Pros: predictable payout, avoids multi-month credits

Option C — Smoothing via committed overage bucket (finance-preferred)
- Create a temporary committed bucket equal to 120% of current avg monthly usage for months 0–2; overage billed at a blended rate (example: 0.75 * list overage rate) for month 3 to allow tail ramping
- Pros: keeps invoices smoother month-to-month without large credit lines

We’ll draft a short term sheet if you confirm the usage numbers. I’ve attached a quick sketch offer (redwood-offer-v1.pdf) and we can follow with a transition-runbook.xlsx showing how we’ll stage prefixes and KV cache priming to avoid extra token churn during cutover.

Best,
Rishi
Sr. Director, Commercial Strategy
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-offer-v1.pdf

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 07:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Vendor change: credits & overage smoothing? — proposed counter options

Team — forwarding Nimbus thread and their stated preference for smoothing-first. Draft proposal below (to bring to the Thurs call). Please review and flag risk items.

Draft counter (three-tiered approach that mixes smoothing + credits):

Tier 1 — Smoothing primary (finance-first, smaller credit):
- Create a Temporary Committed Bucket (TCB) for months 0–2 = 120% of Nimbus's reported avg monthly tokens (from CSV).
- Bill against TCB at the committed unit price (negotiated). Any usage beyond the TCB during months 0–2 billed at blended overage rate = 0.75 * list overage rate.
- Small migration credit: one-time credit equal to 15% of month-1 invoice, payable as invoice credit (non-refundable).
- Clause: If post-cutover production latency or error rate exceeds agreed SLOs for >7 days, customer may request a single additional 10% credit (requires engineering triage confirmation).

Tier 2 — Exit-credit ladder (alternative if they want credit visibility):
- Month 1: 35% service credit; Month 2: 20%; Month 3: 10% (service fees only).
- Redwood reserves right to limit credits to lost ARR threshold and requires a 3-month minimum committed spend to qualify.

Tier 3 — One-time buyout (procurement-preferred simplicity):
- Fixed buyout amount to cover migration services + overlap (example formula: 0.4 * avg 3-month invoice)
- Buyout reduces first-month invoices, no ongoing credits.

Commercial guardrails / packaging notes:
- Attach transition-runbook.xlsx to show opt-in timing for cache priming and prefix migration to minimize token duplication.
- Propose standard A/B rollback window (60 days) where fallback to incumbent is supported but billable according to committed buckets.
- Seats, embedding units, and feature toggles should be separately quoted; credits apply only to inference usage line items.

Risks:
- Over-aggressive credits can create bad precedent; limit to customers that accept a 3-month commit or a minimum ARR threshold.
- Need legal to sign off on SLO-triggered extra-credit clause.

If this looks good I’ll take Tier 1 as our primary position for the call and have Laura run exact numbers from the CSV for their TCB and blended overage figure.

— Rishi

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 08:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Vendor change: credits & overage smoothing? — proposed counter options

Rishi — this is clean. A couple of edits:
- Reduce the migration credit in Tier 1 to 10% (keeps our payback better).
- Make the blended overage cap no worse than 90% of list if their 95th percentile is above the TCB by >30% — protects us if they spike unexpectedly.
- Add a one-time onboarding fee waiver for customers that sign a 12-month commitment (helps offset credit cost).

I’ll run the CSV through our cost model and post numbers shortly. Recommend we loop Monica on the Thurs call to confirm rollout/enablement support and any professional services discounts.

Laura
Commercial Finance
Redwood Inference

Subject: Redwood proposed smoothing-first offer for Nimbus AI (call follow-up)

Kate — thanks for the call earlier. Per discussion our recommended starting position (smoothing-first) is attached as a one-page term summary and the transition runbook. High-level points:

- Temporary Committed Bucket (months 0–2) = 1.2x Nimbus avg monthly tokens (per CSV).
- Blended overage rate for month 3 = 0.75 * list overage rate unless 95th percentile usage > TCB by >30%, in which case blended cap moves to 0.9 * list.
- One-time migration credit = 10% of month-1 invoice, applied as invoice credit.
- 12-month commitment option: waive onboarding fee and reduce migration credit to 5% (improves our payback).
- Inclusion: transition-runbook.xlsx (staging plan, KV priming, cache seeding, rollback steps).

Attachments: redwood-offer-v1.pdf, transition-runbook.xlsx

Next steps: Kate — if this looks reasonable we can convert to a short term sheet and route to legal. Happy to put a PS contact (Monica) on the thread to scope any PS work.

Best,
Rishi
Sr. Director, Commercial Strategy
Redwood Inference
